import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---

# Standardize breed names to handle variations in capitalization and whitespace
df['Rasse1Text'] = df['Rasse1Text'].str.strip().str.title()

# There are many breeds with very few dogs. Let's focus on the most popular ones.
# Find the top 12 most common breeds across all years.
top_breeds = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(12).index

# Filter the DataFrame to only include these top breeds
df_top = df[df['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_breeds)].copy()

# For this visualization, we want to see the age distribution for these top breeds.
# We'll use the dog's age in years. Let's clean it up by removing NaNs.
df_top.dropna(subset=['AlterVHundNum'], inplace=True)
df_top['AlterVHundNum'] = df_top['AlterVHundNum'].astype(int)

# To make the plot readable, let's order the breeds by their median age.
median_ages = df_top.groupby('Rasse1Text')['AlterVHundNum'].median().sort_values()
breed_order = median_ages.index

# --- Visualization ---

# Set the theme and figure size
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))

# Create a boxenplot (enhanced box plot) to show the distribution of ages for each top breed.
# A boxenplot is great for showing more detail in the tails of the distribution.
ax = sns.boxenplot(
    data=df_top,
    x='AlterVHundNum',
    y='Rasse1Text',
    order=breed_order,
    palette='viridis_r',
    linewidth=1.5
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---

# Set a clear title and axis labels
ax.set_title(
    'Age Distribution of the 12 Most Popular Dog Breeds in Zurich',
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    pad=25
)
ax.set_xlabel('Dog Age (Years)', fontsize=14)
ax.set_ylabel('Dog Breed', fontsize=14)

# Customize ticks for better readability
plt.xticks(fontsize=12)
plt.yticks(fontsize=12)

# Ensure the x-axis has integer ticks for years
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))
ax.grid(axis='x', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='-', alpha=0.2)

# Add annotations for median age on each boxenplot
for i, breed in enumerate(breed_order):
    median_val = median_ages[breed]
    ax.text(
        median_val + 0.2,  # x-position (slightly offset from the median line)
        i,                 # y-position (the index of the breed)
        f'{median_val:.1f} yrs', # text to display
        fontdict={
            'horizontalalignment': 'left',
            'size': 11,
            'color': 'black',
            'weight': 'semibold'
        },
        verticalalignment='center'
    )

# Remove the top and right spines for a cleaner look
sns.despine(trim=True, left=True)

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
